steps.text: A Certain Rhodes Island Branch Office, Sargon

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Yep... My brushes, essential oils, and sandpaper strips. All packed away.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Huh? What are you doing in my bag, little bug? Are you coming with me? You can't. Off you go.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Okay! Finished packing.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Wait, no. I need to say goodbye to Mr. Kadeem before I leave.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: That son of a bitch just up and left! Even leaving the stuff behind right next to the door! What the hell's with that?!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: S-Sorry, Mr. Kadeem. I shouldn't have tossed that bug out the door!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Ankhesena? No, don't get me wrong, I'm not talking about you!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: If it's not about me... did something happen?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Eh, it was before you got here. Last month, we had a temporary operator die of his disease. So I packed up his things to ship them back to his family.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: But the moment the local Messenger heard the package belonged to an Infected, he straight up refused to deliver it for me, saying it's bad luck. And that's after I got it all cleaned up so there's no risk of infection.

spans.text: But the moment the local Messenger heard the package belonged to an Infected, he straight up refused to deliver it for me, saying it's bad luck. And that's
I got it all cleaned up so there's no risk of infection.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: B-But you do so many things for the people here. You give out medicine, you treat patients, and even teach them how to prevent getting infected...

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Well, all that's... insignificant compared to the trauma and fear they have of Oripathy.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: *sigh*... I could deliver all this myself if it weren't for this leg. Maybe later.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Alright, forget about it. I see you've finished packing. Are you leaving today?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Yep, I got a message from Rhodes Island two days ago. My sister isn't there, and doesn't want me to go look for her.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It doesn't say why, but I'm sure she has her reasons, and I respect her decision.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: You look real disappointed, though.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I-It's okay. I have my own trials to complete. I can't always be following in my sister's footsteps.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: I'm glad you see it that way. That's a great first step. So do you have any plans or goals for the rest of your trip?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Hm... I haven't thought about where to go. But it's okay. I can think about it on the road.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Hahaha. Come on, let me take your luggage and see you off. I've been real lucky to have you here to help out. Things would've been so much harder with just myself and my bad leg.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: No, no, I enjoyed helping. I'm the one who should be thankful for you taking such good care of me! Speaking of which...

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Eh, don't. No need for all that here.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Mr. Kadeem!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: If this is everything he left behind, I can help you bring them to his family.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Sargon's deserts may be vast and endless, but our tribe has lived in the desert for a long time. We learn how to tread the sands from a very young age.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: And this won't get in the way of your trials?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It won't. Giving others a helping hand is a part of them, too. A really important part!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: If that were coming from anyone else, I would've scoffed.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: But well... You found your way here from a tribe deep in the desert, all by yourself. I have no reason to refuse.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: So? So?!

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: So... I'll let you handle his stuff. Be sure it gets back to his hometown.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: After all, that's the only wish he left us with.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Yeah... got it.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Based on Mr. Kadeem's description, looks like my destination is a pretty isolated tribe... Not sure exactly where it is.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Hm... He did tell me I'd find it if I just follow all the signs after leaving the village.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Really though? I'm not so sure about this... The sign points west to a saxaul forest, and it points east to the red sands there.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Claps hands together) The golden sands, where the setting sun returns. Wheresoever the followers of the gods walk, they will never walk their journey alone.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: O Faceless God, grant me your blessings so that I may successfully cross this desert, allowing a soul that has drifted in the lands for years to return to his homeland.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Time to go.
A breeze blows by. The sign lets out an unbearable creak and softly spins in the wind.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: The sun... The sun has risen again. Have a walked a whole day already? I see nothing but saxauls here. How come I haven't made it to the red sands yet?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Where's the next sign Mr. Kadeem said I'd see? Didn't he say I'd find it after just half a day?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I'm so tired... I can't walk anymore. Let me find some shade to sit down in and get some rest.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: There's no exact location, and the route's already off. How am I supposed to find his hometown?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I wish my sister were here... She'd pet my head and tell me everything's okay.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Lowers head to look at her own hands.)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Hm... I can do this too.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Pats her own head)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It's okay, Ankhesena. Cheer up.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Stay calm. It'll work out somehow. Stand up and take a look at your surroundings. See what clues you can find.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Okay, standing up—

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Waagh!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: O-Ow... I stepped on my clothes.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Oh no, his stuff all spilled out. I gotta pick it back up.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Wah! Don't! Why does the wind have to blow now of all times?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Is this... a diary? I'm sorry, Mister. I didn't mean to look. The wind blew the pages open.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Closes the notebook)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: That short passage just now... Was that a description of his hometown? Maybe... I can find some clues in there.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: O God, please forgive this intrusion against the dead.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Opens the notebook)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'Time and again in my dreams, I make my way home, and my mother stands waiting for me under the date palms. Just like the day she watched me leave my home behind.'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'As my body worsens by the day, I reminisce about that oasis more and more fondly. I left her to chase my dreams, yet I've dreamt of her every night since my departure.'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'The rainy season and the drought season alternate with one another. A small pool of water forms a lake, only for it to dry into a salt marsh just as quickly...'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: He really missed that place. Almost the entire diary is about things that happened in his hometown.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Date palms, an oasis, and a seasonal lake...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: There are little bugs crawling all around here...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Picks one up to closely examine)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I shouldn't be too far from a water source. If luck's on my side, I might even find a settlement there.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Just gotta climb a few sand dunes. Good thing I brought a wooden board to sand ski with.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: *Knock*... Yep... Gotta tie it a bit tighter.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It might get bumpy. I should roll my clothes up. It wouldn't be good if I tripped again.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Three, two, one...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Whoaaaa—!

steps.name: Knowledgeable Old Man
steps.text: The town mentioned here? Let me think... I've been there, but it's been so many years. I can't say for sure if it's still there.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Do you know how to get there, Mister?

steps.name: Knowledgeable Old Man
steps.text: Ride a burdenbeast and keep heading northwest. Once you reach a rock formation that looks like a mushroom, head southwest a few more kilometers, and you should be there.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Do you remember anything about the environment around the town? Are there lots of date palms? Does a lake form when it rains?

steps.name: Knowledgeable Old Man
steps.text: Sorry, that doesn't ring a bell.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'As I almost succumbed to despair, Mr. Kadeem saved me.'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'After a while at the office, my condition started to stabilize, and my mental state has also started to calm...'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Looks like he lived in that office until he died.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: Pffft—

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Huh? Are you hungry? I have some hay here.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Munches)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Look at you eat. Your saliva's getting everywhere.

steps.name: Erudite Woman
steps.text: The place you're looking for is hard to find, Miss. There are a number of oases both big and small to the north of our town, and nearly every one of them has a large field of date palms.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Then... Does the seasonal lake narrow it down?

steps.name: Erudite Woman
steps.text: Not much. Seasonal lakes don't always form in the same place. You can't count on finding anywhere with just that.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: If you don't mind, could you circle where the oases are on this map?

steps.name: Erudite Woman
steps.text: Are you going to check one by one?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Yep, I made a promise, so I'll do it.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'Finally, I made enough money to leave. I don't know what lies beyond this desert, but everything there is new to me. Just that very thought fills me with excitement.'

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: 'I only hope my enthusiasm will bear fruit. Farewell, my homeland.'

steps.name: Desert Merchant
steps.text: Hm, what are you reading, little girl?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It's... someone's past.

steps.name: Desert Merchant
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It's a diary.

steps.name: Desert Merchant
steps.text: Whatever the case, this is your stop. The place you're headed isn't too far from here. We need to be on our way, so this is as far as we can take you.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Thanks for the ride, Mister.

steps.name: Desert Merchant
steps.text: Hahaha, not at all. If you weren't there to save my caravan from the quicksand, I would literally be six feet under right now.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: May the sands bless the rest of your journey!

steps.name: Desert Merchant
steps.text: Haha... thanks!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: This is the last oasis. O Faceless God, please grant me a miracle.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Hello, is anybody home?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Anyone?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: This place looks pretty rundown. Doesn't look like anybody lives here.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Who is it?
Agh!
You entered my tribe's territory without our permission, outblood!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I-I didn't see anyone on my way here. I thought this oasis didn't belong to anybody.
Of course you didn't.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: But why?!
Put down that spear before you ask any questions.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: *Whimpers*... Okay.
(Why is she acting like I wronged her when she was just doing me dirty?)
What are you doing here, outblood?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I was asked to deliver someone's belongings to his homeland.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I have all his things in this bag. Why don't you take a look? If he's not from here, I'll leave immediately.
Bring it over. Let me see.
He's never been back all these years... So he's passed away.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: You knew him?
Right, going by seniority, he was my younger cousin. I took care of his mother before she passed away.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Does he have any other family besides you?
(Shakes head)
Outblood, there aren't a whole lot more people in this tribe. The young ones have all left to make a living. The only ones left are the older folks, and there's less and less of them by the year.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: What will happen to the tribe once everyone's gone?
Do you still not understand, prick? Our tribe will disappear soon. From the oasis, and from Sargon.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Then... What do we do with his things?
I'll bury them next to his mother.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Grips onto her spear uneasily) Now that I delivered these, I... I'll leave now. I won't bother you anymore.
Prick, you're already here. Stay and help me. We only have his things, not his body, but his spirit has returned, and he needs a proper funeral.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Okay, no problem. I-I can help.
Then come with me. We need to get started.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Mister? M-May I ask you a question?
Go ahead.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: If everyone's gone, why do you insist on staying?
Because I'm the tribe's priest. Until the tribe is gone for good, someone has to be here to guard it.
Besides, what if someone wants to come back? Like he did...

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: You want to throw the first dirt, kid?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: M-May I?

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: You're the one who brought him back. You have more than enough right to.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Um, Mr. Kadeem asked me to bring your belongings back to your home, and I made it. Please forgive me for all the accidents that occurred on the road.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: All fruits born on the lands eventually make their way back to the soil, buried and awaiting to sprout anew.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: My dear brother, may you return to your loving mother's embrace. May you find peace under the golden sands. May there never be tears wheresoever you go.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (May he be blessed by the golden sands.)

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: Thanks for helping me. Do you want something to eat? It must have been a tough journey.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: No, no, this kind of journey is nothing out of the ordinary for my tribe.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: I've never left this oasis. I can't imagine how your desert tribe lives. Just looking at the tumbling sands makes me afraid.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: There's nothing to be afraid of. A god lives in the desert, and He protects us.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: We used to believe the forest had a god too, and it was thanks to Him that our tribe managed to survive and prosper, but it looks like we've been abandoned.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Of course not. Gods don't abandon their children.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: But what if His children abandoned their faith in Him?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: You mean those who left...?

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: Did he live a good life outside?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Not really. He got infected with an incurable disease. Rocks grew on his body. It hurt, and could spread to other people. He would've been ostracized in lots of places.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: Did it hurt when he died?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I don't know. He had already passed away by the time I got there... But Mr. Kadeem was there to take care of him, so he probably died peacefully. At the very least, he wasn't alone.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: And who's Mr. Kadeem?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Mr. Kadeem's in charge of the place where he worked. He's very experienced when it comes to treating Oripathy.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: I used to complain that he never came back to see his own mother one last time. He mentioned in his letter that it'd only take a day of travel on foot to get back here from where he settled down.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Was it... that close? *Whimper*... To tell the truth, I got lost on my way here. It took me half a month to find this place.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: Perhaps he traveled somewhere else after he sent that letter.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: But now that I've heard what happened, I can understand why he wasn't willing to come back.

steps.name: Tribe Priest
steps.text: Nobody here's ever come down with a disease like that. I wouldn't be able to do anything for his pain here, and if he spread it to others, I'd have no way to deal with that.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: So...
Ankhesena opens her mouth only to find herself unable to say what she was going to say.
Once someone has set their mind on crossing a desert, they can no longer turn back. Because the sands that blow with the wind will undoubtedly swallow the path they'd taken.
And the courage they took so long to gather is never enough for them to look back at their unrecognizable past.

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: *Sigh*—

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: Old fool, stop sighing in front of the kids. You'll bring them bad luck.

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: You dare call me old with that white beard of yours? Take a look yourself. The ones who came back from their journeys this year are just half that of last year. What should we do if this keeps happening?

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: Who am I to influence how they think? Once they've experienced all the amazing things outside, who would come back here to live a life of nothing?

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: And how can you be so unbothered by that? The tribe will collapse one day if this keeps up.

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: I'm at my wits' end too, but we can't just keep the children here and not let them leave.

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: (Shakes head helplessly)

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: Right, I have something I need to discuss with you. I got a letter a few days ago, and I'm worried about what it says.

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: A child caught that disease and wants to come back...

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: That's a good thing. They should.

steps.name: Tribe Elder
steps.text: He said he's infected with an incurable disease, and he's worried about spreading it to others in the tribe... But I can't bear seeing one of our children stranded out there.

steps.name: Worried Elder
steps.text: What should we do?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Tugs Carnelian's sleeve)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Sis...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: What's wrong, Ankhesena?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: You'll go on your journey in a year. Will you come back after you leave?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Of course I will, it's just...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: Sis?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I don't know what He has in mind for me. What if He doesn't want me to stay here?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: No... Once you leave, I'll keep praying to Him. Wherever His children walk, they are bound to be far from evil.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: That's not evil, Ankhesena. It's not...

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: It's me, Mr. Kadeem. Ankhesena. Could you open the door, please?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Coming, coming.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: I thought you were on your journey? Did you manage to deliver his things?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: *pant*—*pant*—

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Maybe you should come in and catch your breath first. Here, have some water.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I did...

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: (Glug-glug)

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: And I gave him a proper burial with the priest there.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: That's great, but you didn't come all the way back here to tell me that, did you?

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Look at you. You're covered in sweat. Didn't I say you didn't have to come back?

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: That's not why. I found it. I found what it is that I want to do.

steps.name: Office Operator
steps.text: Hahaha, so you found a goal for your journey? Go on then, don't keep me in suspense.

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: I want to go to Rhodes Island. I want to go to the landship!

steps.name: Ankhesena
steps.text: There are things there that I want to bring back to my tribe.
She said those words in a sonorous, powerful way, completely unlike the soft voice she usually speaks in. Like the heavy, blazing sunset crushing the yellow desert outside the window.
And under the sunset's glow, the mark on her forehead glows ever radiant.
